The Netto & Magin Letter 
On 29 July 2025, Netto and Luke hand-delivered the Netto & Magin Letter

The Netto & Magin Letter enclosed a “General Notice to Enforcement 
Respondent” against Sole Relief. It went further than simply notifying the 
landlord (which in itself is abnormal) but it included a threatening ultimatum in 
4
paragraphs 6 and 7, suggesting that adjacent unnumbered units shall be deemed 
to belong to Sole Relief and thereby subjected to enforcement proceedings.  
8. 
The Netto & Magin Letter is highly unusual and improper for the following 
reasons: 
Highly irregular and contrary to ordinary practice  
It is contrary to ordinary practice for law firms to send enforcement orders to 
landlords, let alone by hand-delivered letters. Enforcement procedures are 
ordinarily directed to the Sheriff’s Office and executed without prior notice. 
Purpose of enforcement orders 
The purpose of an enforcement order is to enable the Sheriff to effect seizure of 
property swiftly and without advance warning. There is no logical purpose in 
notifying a landlord in advance of such enforcement. 
Inference of malice 
The only reasonable inference is that the purpose of the Netto & Magin Letter 
was to shame and humiliate Sole Relief and to cause difficulties with its landlord 
Ibis Hotel Imperial Lavender / GPHL.  
5
This aligns with the pattern of the three vexatious striking out applications, the 
Intentional Humiliation Episode and the Surreptitious EJD Episode. 
Exceeding the scope of the order  
The enforcement order DC/EO 107/2025 authorises the Sheriff to seize property 
at 28 Penhas Road #01-03. There is no authorisation to extend enforcement to 
adjacent unnumbered units. 
Yet in paragraphs 4–6 of the Netto & Magin Letter, Netto asserted that seizure 
would extend to “adjacent units without numbering.” 
Improper demand to landlord   
Netto went further to demand that GP Hotel Capital Pte Ltd prove within 14 days 
that the adjacent units did not belong to our clients. This is unreasonable and 
baseless since landlords are not responsible for enforcement proceedings, nor are 
they required to provide such proof. 
Lack of bona fides   
Taken together, the contents and delivery of the Netto & Magin Letter 
demonstrate that it was not issued in good faith for the purpose of legitimate 
enforcement. Rather, it was calculated to humiliate and harass Sole Relief and to 
6
alarm its landlord, with the ulterior motive of destabilising their tenancy and 
damaging their business reputation.

The tone and content of the Netto & Magin Letter were highly abnormal for 
lawyers acting in bona fide enforcement. Enforcement in Singapore is strictly 
regulated. Enforcement orders are executed by the Sheriff and Examinations of 
Judgment Debtor are conducted under oath before a Registrar. None of these 
enforcement avenues permits a solicitor to utilise enforcement documents to 
threaten and alarm a non-party landlord. 
A non-party landlord such as GPHL is under no duty to “prove” anything to 
judgment creditors or their solicitors, much less whether adjacent unnumbered 
units belonged to their tenants. The Netto & Magin Letter, which demanded such 
“proof” and threatened disruption of hotel operations and alarm hotel guests, was 
outside all established enforcement channels and was plainly calculated to alarm 
the landlord.

publicly listed hotel group are compelled to intervene, it shows how alarming the 
letter was given that enforcement action at a hotel will invariably disrupt hotel 
operations.
